key_insight: PRISM-CAFO uses an infrastructure-first, prior-conditioned and explainable pipeline to identify and characterize CAFOs from aerial and satellite imagery, enabling accurate, interpretable, and scalable mapping of large livestock operations.
problem_solved: Provides a reproducible method to detect and map concentrated animal feeding operations (CAFOs) at scale from remote imagery, addressing challenges of accuracy, interpretability, and rapid large-area coverage for environmental and public-health monitoring.
method: Prior-conditioned segmentation: incorporate infrastructure priors (e.g., barns, lagoons, roads) into multi-resolution models to focus detection on CAFO-relevant features.

Explainable aggregation: rule-based and interpretable post-processing links detected infrastructure components into CAFO footprints and derives attribute-level characterizations (size, density, risk proxies).
Scalable pipeline: end-to-end remote-sensing workflow for large-area inference, quality control, and exportable maps suitable for downstream analysis and decision making.
impact: Shows how domain priors and explainability improve geospatial model utility and trust, offering AI/ML practitioners a transferable approach for facility detection and environmental monitoring that balances performance, interpretability, and scalability.
visual_elements: Pipeline flow diagram: input imagery → prior-conditioned segmentation → explainable aggregation → final CAFO map
Before/after satellite panels: raw imagery vs. overlayed detected infrastructure and CAFO footprints
Component map: icon-based legend showing detected barns, lagoons, roads and how they combine into CAFOs
Performance/coverage chart: precision/recall or area-mapped vs. baseline to show scalability and accuracy gains
paper_title: PRISM-CAFO: Prior-conditioned Remote-sensing Infrastructure Segmentation and Mapping for CAFOs
paper_authors: Oishee Bintey Hoque, Nibir Chandra Mandal, Kyle Luong, Amanda Wilson, Samarth Swarup
